thesis: **Both of my invalidations fired today, and this is the cleanest kill of the run.** Every XLE memo since 9 September has said a confirmed reopening of Hormuz transits voids the thesis regardless of price. US Central Command now reports flows through the Strait at a **six-month high with the main lanes clear of mines**, and Saudi throughput has gone from 700,000 bpd in August to **2.8 mb/d over six days**. Separately the price level fired: XLE closed **62.75, below the 62.85 stop** I have named in every memo. The scarcity premium this position was bought for no longer exists.
bull_case:
Pattern analyst: setup is a **failed breakout, now broken** - close 62.75 against a 52-week high made twelve days ago, RSI down to 44 from 74 on 15 September, 63d momentum +16.1%, and price **below the trailing stop at 62.85**. Squeeze 0.98. Verdict: pattern is against entry; the structure that supported this is gone.

What is left of the case: Brent at $100 is still historically high, the majors' cash flows are priced off a strip well above their budget assumptions, Exxon and Chevron remain 42.5% of the fund, and diplomacy can fail - Trump only says he is *probably* open to meeting Pezeshkian. If the UNGA meeting produces nothing, the premium can return as fast as it left.
bear_case: The supply emergency is over in substance. Six-month-high flows, clear transit lanes and a 4x recovery in Saudi throughput are not a headline - they are the physical condition the whole trade was short. Brent has fallen four straight sessions to $100.06 and the forecasters were already below spot: the EIA at about $90/b for 2H26 and Goldman at $85 for December. The position is -4.5%, the worst in the book, and below its stop. Macro, once for the day: **Brent fell to $100.06, down 3.67% and a fourth straight losing session**, because US Central Command says crude and LNG flows through the Strait of Hormuz have reached a **six-month high with the main transit lanes clear of mines**, and satellite imagery shows Saudi Arabia moving **2.8 mb/d through the Strait over six days against 700,000 bpd in August**. Trump says he is probably open to meeting President Pezeshkian at the UN General Assembly this week. Falling oil pushed the 10-year yield back below 5% and lit a risk-on move: about **$648M of short positions were force-closed**. Bitcoin is at an 8-month high, up 44% on the quarter. The Fed raised 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 16 September with one more penciled for 2026. A rate path with one more hike penciled in is a demand headwind on top. Desk record (research/outcomes.json): 12 closed trades, 0 wins, -$168.00 realised. Long memos 9 good of 13 judged (0.69); skip decisions 1 of 34 (0.03) - the skip number is the desk's flat calls being marked against a crypto sleeve that has run without it, and it is the more honest of the two.

Weekly Hormuz transit volumes from CENTCOM

Brent down four straight sessions to $100.06
EIA ~$90/b and Goldman $85 for December, both below spot

invalidation: The pattern analyst's level is **62.85**, the trailing stop carried in the packet, and price has already closed below it - this is the invalidation, not a warning of one. It would become interesting again only on a confirmed breakdown in Hormuz diplomacy **and** a reclaim of 65.74, the old high.
